Author: Rajendra Kumar Srivastava
Bench: Rajendra Kumar Srivastava
 1 Mcrc-35263-2019
 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 Mcrc-35263-2019
 (Dipankar Ganguly Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh)
2
Jabalpur, Dated : 06-09-2019
Shri Sandeep Mahawar, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Sharad Singh Baghel, learned P.L. for the respondent No.1/State.
Record from the Office of Food Safety Administration Department, Khandwa, District-Khandwa be called for in respect of applicant/accused.

entities.text: Office of Food Safety Administration Department,
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: This Miscellaneous Criminal Case has been filed by the applicant/petitioner under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. for setting aside the impugned order dated 12.03.2019 passed by learned III Additional Sessions Judge, Khandwa in Criminal Revision No.42/2018 whereby the learned III Additional Sessions Judge has rejected the petition present by the present applicant/petitioner.
Issue notice to the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 on payment of process fee within a period of seven working days by registered A/D as well as ordinary mode.
Notices be made returnable within a period of two weeks.
Heard on IA.No.15792/2019 an application for staying the proceedings of Criminal Case No.2658/2013 pending before Judicial Magistrate First Class Khandwa, District-Khandwa.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class Khandwa, District-Khandwa
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant/petitioner submits that respondent No.1 has filed a complaint under Sections 26(1), 26(1)(11), Section 27(1)(2c) read with Section 51, Section 59 (1) of Food Safety and Standard Acts, 2006 against him before learned trial Court.

He also submits that according to the respondents, the incident was occurred on 17.01.2012 and complaint was filed by the respondents on 25.08.2013, thereafter learned trial Court took cognizance against the applicant/petitioner, but the order of cognizance is against the provisions of Section 77 of the Food Safety and Standard Acts, 2006.

Section 77 of the Food Safety and Standard Acts, 2006 is prescribed 2 MCRC-35263-2019 time limit for the prosecution and in which it is held that "no court shall take cognizance of an offence under this Act after the expiry of the period of one year from the date of commission of an offence".
So, in this provisions, complaint is time barred, therefore no further proceedings can be stayed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is evident that Proviso of Section 77 of the Food Safety and Standard Acts, 2006 is prescribed that the "Commissioner of Food Safety may, for reasons to be recorded in writing, approve prosecution within an extended period of upto three years" and learned trial Court has considered this proviso in the impugned order.
So, at this state, it is not an appropriate to stay the proceeding in Criminal Case No.2658/2013 pending before Judicial Magistrate First Class Khandwa, District-Khandwa.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class Khandwa, District-Khandwa
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Accordingly, IA.No.15792/2019 is hereby dismissed.

In the meantime, it is directed that the trial Court i.e. Judicial Magistrate First Class, Khandwa shall proceed further in the proceedings in Criminal Case No.2658/2013, but the final judgment shall not be pronounced till the next date of hearing.
List the matter after three weeks.
(RAJENDRA KUMAR SRIVASTAVA) JUDGE sp SAVITRI PATEL 2019.09.11 10:37:26 +05'30'
